leads.title: Lawrence v. Texas, U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Struck down all state sodomy laws, making same-sex sexual activity legal in Florida.
leads.detail: Cited as 'U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Lawrence v. Texas on June 26, 2003' - state sodomy law unenforceable though not repealed as of 2020

leads.title: Brenner v. Scott, U.S. District Court
leads.documents: Ruled Florida's same-sex marriage ban unconstitutional; marriage legal since injunction took effect.
leads.detail: Cited as 'ruled on August 21, 2014, in Brenner v. Scott, that Florida's same-sex marriage ban was in violation of the Constitution' - Judge Robert Lewis Hinkle quote, effective January 6, 2015

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Workplace discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is discrimination on basis of sex under Title VII.
leads.detail: Cited as 'On June 15, 2020, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Bostock v. Clayton County, consolidated with Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda, and R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission'

leads.title: Glenn v. Brumby, U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
leads.documents: Employment discrimination based on transgender status is tantamount to discrimination on basis of sex under Civil Rights Act of 1964.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In December 2011, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit (which covers Alabama, Florida and Georgia) ruled that Vandy Beth Glenn... had been unfairly terminated... due to her transgender status'

leads.title: Florida Commission on Human Relations announcement
leads.documents: State civil rights enforcement agency will enforce Bostock to investigate discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In February 2021, the Florida Commission on Human Relations, the state's civil rights enforcement agency, announced it will enforce the Bostock ruling' with Human Rights Campaign quote hailing decision

leads.title: Equality Florida travel advisory
leads.documents: LGBTQ advocacy group advisory to avoid visiting or moving to Florida due to legislation.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In April 2023, Florida LGBTQ advocacy group Equality Florida issued a travel advisory for LGBTQ people to avoid visiting or moving to the state'

leads.title: Human Rights Campaign travel advisory
leads.documents: National human-rights report signing onto travel advisory, citing legislation recently signed by Governor DeSantis.
leads.detail: Cited as 'The following May, the Human Rights Campaign signed on to the travel advisory, citing legislation recently signed by Governor DeSantis, while stopping short of calling for a boycott'

leads.title: Florida Senate Bill 254 (2023)
leads.documents: Law allowing child custody modifications on basis that child has received, or might receive, gender-affirming care; codifies ban on gender-affirming care for minors.
leads.detail: Cited as 'On May 17, 2023, DeSantis signed Florida Senate Bill 254, as passed by the state legislature, which will allow child custody modifications' and 'In April 2023, both houses... passed a bill codifying the ban... and allowing the state to modify or nullify parental custody agreements from other states'

leads.title: Florida Facility Requirements Based on Sex Act / Bathroom Bill (2023) and Board of Education procedures
leads.documents: Makes it illegal for trans person at state school, university, or government building to use bathroom consistent with gender identity; criminal trespass charge; disciplinary procedures including firing.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Since July 1, 2023, it is illegal for a trans person at any state school, state university, or government building... to use any bathroom' - 'On May 17, 2023, DeSantis signed a bathroom bill into law' - 'On August 23, for Florida's 28 public community and state colleges, the Florida Board of Education approved a disciplinary procedure: employees... can be fired' - 'On October 18, 2023, the Florida Board of Education voted to apply similar restriction... at private college and university buildings'

leads.title: Florida Board of Medicine and Board of Osteopathic Medicine rules on gender-affirming care
leads.documents: State-issued rules banning gender-affirming healthcare for minors and requiring 24-hour waiting period / Board approval for adults; codified May 17, 2023 law.
leads.detail: Cited as 'On October 31, 2022, the Florida Medical Board implemented the new rule requiring a 24-hour waiting period for adults... and to ban minors' - 'On November 4, 2022, the new rule was approved by the Florida Board of Medicine' - 'The Board of Medicine rule took effect on March 16, 2023' - 'On May 17, 2023, DeSantis signed a law to codify these changes' with Surgeon General Joseph Ladapo April 2022 press release background
